blocks.prompt: 15. An AC source supplies a voltage of \(V = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) volts to a circuit with impedance \(Z = \frac{1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ohms. Calculate the current in polar form.
blocks.explanation: Yeh real life application hai: AC circuits ka Ohm's law, \(V = IZ\) (jaise kitab ki Example 17 mein). V voltage hai, I current aur Z impedance (AC circuit mein current ki rukawat, jo complex number hoti hai). V aur Z diye hain, humein current \(I = V/Z\) polar form mein chahiye. Plan: Z ko bhi polar form mein badlein, kyunke taqseem polar form mein sab se aasaan hai: moduli taqseem, arguments minus.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(V = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\) volts, \(Z = \frac{1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}\) ohms.
To find (maloom karna hai): current \(I\) polar form mein.
Method (tareeqa): \(V = IZ\), is liye \(I = \frac{V}{Z}\); V pehle hi polar form mein hai, Z ko bhi kar lein.

Qadam 1: Z ka modulus
\[Z = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\]
\[|Z| = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{4} + \tfrac{3}{4}} = 1\]
Kyun: pehle Z ko alag parts mein likha, phir \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\).

Qadam 2: Z ka argument
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2} = \sqrt{3}\]
\[\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[Z = \cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: dono parts positive hain, is liye Z first quadrant mein hai aur \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}\) hi sahi angle hai. Yeh wohi number hai jo Sawal 2(iii) mein tha.

Qadam 3: Taqseem karein
\[I = \dfrac{120}{1}\,(\cos\phi + i\sin\phi)\]
\[\phi = \tfrac{\pi}{4} - \tfrac{\pi}{3} = \tfrac{3\pi - 4\pi}{12}\]
\[\phi = -\tfrac{\pi}{12}\]
\[I = 120\left[\cos\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right) + i\sin\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\right]\]
Kyun: quotient rule: moduli taqseem (\(120 \div 1\)), arguments minus (V ka angle minus Z ka angle). Common denominator 12 liya: \(\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{3\pi}{12}\), \(\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{12}\).

Qadam 4: Signs saaf karein
\[I = 120\left(\cos\tfrac{\pi}{12} - i\sin\tfrac{\pi}{12}\right)\]
\[I \approx 115.91 - 31.06i\]
Kyun: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\). Yeh answer key ki form se milta hai. Negative argument ka matlab hai ke current voltage se thora 'peeche' (lag) hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(IZ\) se V wapas aana chahiye.
\[IZ = 120 \cdot 1\,[\cos(-\tfrac{\pi}{12} + \tfrac{\pi}{3}) + i\sin(\cdots)]\]
\[-\tfrac{\pi}{12} + \tfrac{4\pi}{12} = \tfrac{3\pi}{12} = \tfrac{\pi}{4}\]
Is liye \(IZ = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = V\). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(I = 120\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{12} - i\sin\frac{\pi}{12}\right)\) amperes, yani modulus 120 A aur argument \(-\frac{\pi}{12}\) (\(\approx 115.91 - 31.06i\)).
